description: The National Estuarine Research Reserve “Planning for Climate Change” Workshop is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Climate Adaptation Knowledge Exchange (CAKE); Padilla Bay Reserve; Washington Department of Ecology. Pilot workshops were conducted in March 2009 to educate and train coastal managers and planners in Washington State on climate change impacts and adaptation strategies. Coverage: King County, WA (2009). The toolkit gives King County, WA as the location, 2009 as the year and 2 months as the duration. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.

outcomes: The project was completed in June 2009. The Padilla Bay NERR continues to design and conduct workshops and trainings around climate science. Additionally, the NERR site is used by the Washington Department of Ecology’s Coastal Training Program, which provides practical, science-based training to professionals who make decisions about shoreline management.
